decision: sweep.py main and worldseed --write now ask the halt before writing; corpus_db --rebuild stays un-interlocked.
how: FOR interlocking: CHARACTER_SWEEP.json is read as fact by magnitude, standards, foreman and hostcheck, and WORLDSEEDS.json is the roster six modules build on, so writing them while a halt stands feeds trusted consumers from state the halt calls untrustworthy; the twenty-module roster's stated rule is 'every hand-run tool that writes the corpus or the library's output'. AGAINST: both are rebuildable derived files. Decided for those two because their consumers treat them as fact and adding the check is a tightening with no cost. Both use the ingest_doc pattern (fail-closed on the escalation import, writing path only; worldseed preview without --write and sweep's read-only pieces are not gated; --limit --write still refuses with rc 2 first). corpus_db --rebuild KEPT off the roster: state/corpus.db is a derived index every result labels as a stale FLOOR, nothing consumes it as fact, and it is the tool a person reaches for to investigate during a halt, so gating it would obstruct diagnosis for no safety gain. The opposite view (the ruling's wording is 'every tool that writes') loses because that rule is about corpus and output files, not a self-declared-stale scratch index.

decision: register() now lands WIKI_HOSTS.json through a digest-before-read compare-and-swap with a bounded retry.
how: AGAINST: hand-run once per book, and the read-to-write window is microseconds. FOR: it is the one file the project cannot rebuild, hostcheck and scout write it on their own clocks, a lost update is silent, and the loop is about fifteen lines using silence.digest_of and replace_if_unchanged. Not routed through hostcheck._land_hosts because that writes feats.HOSTS while this module's HOSTS is what the existing halt net redirects, so the call would have written the real file from that net. A refused swap re-reads and re-decides (a live wiki still outranks doc:); five refusals return None as before.

decision: An unassayed best band is a legitimate terminal synthesis and stays merged as it is.
how: AGAINST (keep unchanged): the band is an honest value, not a hole -- the pipeline's own phase_synthesis writes the same thing when evidence fails valid_scale_note, and Hard Rule 3 prefers 'unassayed' to an invented band. FOR (list it as outstanding): the source ends up with no ceiling. But that is a property of its evidence, which a repeat model call does not change, so listing it in stranded_sources() would make the rescue tool re-run the same call forever. This function's docstring already records five drifts from pipeline; making retry diverge from pipeline here would add a sixth. No change; if the owner wants unassayed sources surfaced, that belongs in a report, not in the retry selector.

decision: binding_health canary titles now skip excluded (struck) entries; tuning's stale-proof handling is kept.
how: binding_health: a struck entry was struck because it is not a real thing, so it is the title most likely to be absent from the wiki; probing it as believed-present can read a healthy host as failing and quarantine it. Skipping it only removes bad probe inputs, and a dead host fails on every title, so detection is not loosened. Applied in both known_present_titles and known_present_title. tuning POOL_PROOF stale: KEPT. AGAINST keeping: a stale proof can claim buckets that have since died. FOR keeping: the code already says so in the reason string, and regime() also requires a measured success rate once MIN_CALLS_TO_JUDGE calls exist, so a wrongly-trusted cloud regime generates the very calls that judge it within one RECHECK window and falls back; zeroing a stale proof would drop to 2 local workers whenever the proof job is late, a large and persistent throughput loss for a self-correcting risk. The proof file was refreshed today.
